claims.text: The 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock deposited under standard thermal-spray parameters produces a coating below the required thickness.
Increasing flame temperature by adjusting the fuel/oxygen ratio will increase feedstock-particle temperature.
Higher particle temperature will produce more complete melting of the FeCoNiCrAl particles before impact.
More complete particle melting will improve spreading on the substrate.
More complete particle melting will improve bonding and inter-splat cohesion.
Improved particle melting and inter-splat cohesion will increase deposition efficiency.
Increased deposition efficiency will increase the deposition rate and coating thickness.
The higher-temperature process will produce a denser coating than the baseline process.
The coating deposited at increased flame temperature will exceed the thickness obtained from the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline under standard flame conditions.
The increased-temperature process will retain the required coating integrity.
A controlled shielding atmosphere will limit oxidation during deposition.
Shielding gas will minimize oxidation during rapid quenching of the sprayed droplets.
The increased-temperature coating will exhibit minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
Moderate flame-temperature increases within the normal thermal-spray operating range will improve melting without adverse side effects.
Excessively high flame temperatures may cause uncontrolled oxidation.
Excessively high flame temperatures may cause phase instabilities in the coating.
